title: Deterministic Verification and a Single-Repair Guardrail for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: a Paired, Shared‑Candidate Study
abstract: We report a sealed, preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal verifier-detected effect of interposing a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the same LLM-generated configuration candidate. Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused for both baseline and guarded episodes) we produced one candidate per natural-language intent with gpt-5-mini for N = 250 pairs and evaluated two episodes per intent: baseline (accept candidate) and guarded (deterministic_netops_validator_v5; if failing, permit one automated repair). Execution completed the preregistered confirmatory partition (500 episodes) with model_calls_used = 251. Results: baseline verifier-pass 249/250 (99.6%), guarded verifier-pass 250/250 (100.0%); contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = +0.4 percentage points, 95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp] (paired bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The single discordant pair was converted to pass by the single permitted repair. The reported confirmatory estimand and inference apply only to the executed synthetic/emulation partition; the preregistered sim‑to‑real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed in this run. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the study evidence bundle referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being explored as intent-to-configuration translators in network operations (NetOps), offering automated drafting of device CLI sequences from operator intents. Stochastic generation, however, creates operational risk: syntax errors, incorrect command ordering, local-policy violations, and vendor-CLI subtleties can produce unsafe or non-functional changes. A common mitigation architecture inserts a deterministic validator between generation and acceptance and may attempt bounded automated repair — a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pattern — accepting only validator-passed candidates or attempting limited repair when mechanically verifiable defects are detected. Prior surveys and empirical studies document feasibility of draft-configuration generation while emphasizing the need for deterministic verification or human oversight [1],[2].

This work asks a tightly scoped, preregistered question: when the same initial LLM candidate is reused for both arms (shared_initial_candidate), what is the marginal verifier-detected improvement from interposing a deterministic validator plus at most one template-driven automated repair? By design, the paired shared-candidate design isolates the validator-and-single-repair marginal effect on identical generated outputs rather than conflating differences due to independent generation. We executed the preregistered confirmatory partition (N_pairs = 250) and report artifact-grounded counts, exact paired inference, bootstrap confidence intervals, and a concise failure analysis. Our contribution is an auditable, artifact-backed bound on the marginal verifier+single-repair effect for a constrained NetOps task bank under shared_initial_candidate semantics.
sections.related_work:
Prior NetOps and LLM literature motivates validator-augmented pipelines and clarifies limits of LLM-only self-correction. Recent NetOps-focused evaluations show LLMs can produce usable draft configurations under controlled conditions, but often require verification and repair for mechanical defects [3],[4]. Deterministic verification tools (e.g., model-checking and configuration-analysis systems) are established methods for checking forwarding/reachability and many local-policy properties and are used as validators in GVR pipelines [5]. Generate-and-verify and program-repair workflows have been shown to reduce mechanically checkable error classes in code and configuration domains, though deeper semantic correctness and vendor heterogeneity remain challenging [6]. Security analyses of prompt-injection demonstrate realistic threats to LLM-integrated applications and motivate layered defenses including validators and artifact filtering [7].

This study differs in three ways: (i) a preregistered paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics that isolates validator/repair marginal effects on identical model outputs; (ii) complete provider-call reconciliation across pipeline stages (shared initial generation and a single permitted repair) so the marginal cost of repair stages is auditable; and (iii) archival of validator traces and analysis artifacts enabling reproduction of the reported numeric bounds.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration, estimand, and semantics. The experiment was preregistered (study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1) as a confirmatory paired design with N_pairs = 250, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, and primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The preregistration froze the single-repair policy (≤1 automated repair per episode), exclusion/contamination rules, analysis tests (exact McNemar two-sided; paired-bootstrap percentile CIs), and maximum model-call budget. The preregistration artifact SHA-256 is recorded in the evidence bundle (see Disclosure).

Task bank and constraints. A deterministic task generator produced 250 constrained intent tasks. Each task encoded an initial_state, expected_final_state, a required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow constraints (e.g., make-before-break switchover, paired-link atomic MTU changes, protected interfaces). Tasks were intentionally constrained to exercise ordering and local-workflow invariants while limiting natural-language ambiguity; the full task manifest and task payload schema are archived in the evidence bundle.

Model and pipeline semantics. The declared model for all initial generations was gpt-5-mini. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics exactly one initial generation was produced per intent; that candidate was reused for both the baseline episode (accept candidate) and the guarded episode (deterministic validation and optional single repair). The guarded pipeline submitted the candidate to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementing full_intent_constraint_validation: CLI parsing, required_sequence checking, workflow-constraint enforcement, and deterministic final_state snapshot comparison to the task-encoded expectation. When validator valid = false, the pipeline permitted up to one deterministic template-driven repair that targeted syntactic and ordering defects (reordering commands to required_sequence, splitting/formatting adjustments); repaired candidates were re-submitted to the same validator. No multi-iteration repair or human escalation was permitted by design.

Inclusion, contamination, and analysis plan. The preregistration excluded items that failed vendor-parsers preventing deterministic verification or that contained denylisted credential-like tokens; contamination detectors flagged instruction-like embedded tokens for sensitivity analyses. The primary analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1: an exact McNemar two-sided test on paired binary validator outcomes and a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the guarded − baseline paired difference (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). The analysis plan and sensitivity treatments (treating excluded items as failures, contamination treatments) were preserved and executed as registered.
sections.results:
Execution and reconciliation. The preregistered confirmatory partition completed as planned: planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, complete_pair_count = 250. Provider-call accounting reconciled to the shared-initial design: the run used one initial generation per intent and exercised one repair-generation call in total; aggregated model_calls_used = 251. All reconciliation artifacts and the stage-level audit are archived in the evidence bundle.

Primary outcomes and contingency. Deterministic validator scoring returned baseline_success_count = 249/250 (baseline_success_rate = 0.996) and guarded_success_count = 250/250 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). The observed paired contingency table is n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0, i.e., a single discordant pair converted from fail→pass by the single permitted repair. The repair-conversion rate on the confirmatory partition is 1/250 = 0.4%.

Statistical inference. The exact two-sided McNemar test on discordant counts (n10 = 1, n01 = 0) returned p = 1.0. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the guarded − baseline paired difference (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) is [0.0, 0.012] in absolute fraction units (i.e., 0 – 1.2 percentage points). These numeric analysis artifacts and the contingency table are archived for audit.

Representative validator diagnostics and repairs. For passed episodes the validator reported parsed_command_count and required_command_count matching the task-required_sequence; representative artifacts show correct ordering and normalized configurations for medium/hard tasks (examples archived). Only one automated repair was invoked; its trace shows a deterministic ordering/syntactic correction that resolved the validator violation and produced a guarded-pass for that pair. No episodes were excluded for contamination or parser-blocking errors in the confirmatory partition.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation of the near‑null marginal effect. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and the constrained synthetic/emulation partition, the marginal verifier-detected benefit of a deterministic validator plus a single template-driven repair was small: initial gpt-5-mini candidates satisfied the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases and the guarded pipeline converted the single failing candidate via the solitary permitted repair. The paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (1.2 percentage points) is an artifact-grounded empirical bound on verifier-improvement for this task scope and run.

Why the observed gain is small (artifact-grounded factors). Three run-supported factors account for the modest observed marginal gain: (1) the deterministic task generator encoded constrained intents and allowed_touched_fields that reduced ambiguity and favored well-formed CLI sequences; (2) gpt-5-mini produced highly consistent, syntactically well-formed sequences for these constrained intents; and (3) the deterministic validator checks mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, and expected_final_state snapshots) and does not measure broader behavioral correctness in live protocol execution or cross-device emergent interactions.

Power, assumptions, and limits to inference. The preregistered power calculation had assumed a baseline pass rate ≈ 0.90 when choosing N_pairs = 250 to detect an absolute 15 pp effect. The realized baseline pass rate (0.996) was much higher than assumed, reducing power to detect small absolute improvements; hence the bootstrap CI is the more informative practical bound. Crucially, the executed confirmatory estimand applies only to the synthetic/emulation partition: the preregistered sim-to-real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed and remains unsettled.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: outcomes depend on prompt templates, shared_initial_candidate semantics, the single-repair policy, and the validator encoding. Construct validity: the deterministic validator measures mechanically verifiable correctness but does not assert live protocol-level correctness. External validity: the confirmatory evidence covers only the synthetic/emulation partition with one declared model and one validator; results do not establish multi-model, adversarial, or large-scale production generality. Security: adaptive prompt-injection and retrieval-based adversaries were not exercised here and remain open threats.

Operational implications. In tightly constrained emulation-style tasks with a capable LLM, a single deterministic validator plus one template-driven repair may yield only marginal verifier-detected improvement because initial candidates are often already validator-conforming. This should not be generalized to broader operational contexts: stronger, broader validators, multi-iteration repair, human-in-the-loop escalation, production heterogeneity, or adversarial conditions could materially change the benefit calculus.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed, preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics to quantify the marginal verifier-detected effect of inserting a deterministic validator plus one automated repair on identical LLM-generated configuration candidates. In N = 250 constrained synthetic intents with gpt-5-mini, initial candidates passed the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases; the guarded pipeline converted the single failing candidate via the single permitted repair. Observed paired improvement = 0.4 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp]; p = 1.0). We explicitly disclose that the preregistered sim‑to‑real confirmatory comparison was not executed and that the executed confirmatory estimand is limited to the synthetic/emulation partition. Broader production, adversarial, multi-model, and multi-iteration repair evaluations remain necessary to establish generality. All execution and analysis artifacts referenced in this paper are archived in the study evidence bundle described in the Disclosure Statement.

disclosure_statement:
Human role and autonomy boundary: After the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher autonomy lock, the autonomous system performed literature search, study selection, preregistration freeze, prompt preservation, model calls, deterministic validation, permitted repair execution, analysis, drafting, peer-review, revision, and finalization without manual human editing of technical content. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and conducted pre-lock infrastructure development; no human manually edited manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.

Models, tools, and framework: declared model = gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses); deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. The run used a guarded generate–verify–repair flow permitting at most one automated repair per episode, as specified in the preregistration.

Preregistration and immutable prompt reference: preregistration study id = study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 (preregistration SHA-256: 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede). Immutable master prompt used to initiate the autonomous run: provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. The full execution and analysis evidence bundle (execution manifest and artifact hash manifest) is archived with the study and is referenced by the preregistration identifier above. Interested readers can use the preregistration manifest to locate the archived execution and analysis artifacts; the study archive contains raw model responses, task manifests, deterministic validator traces, repair traces, the deterministic reconciliation audit, and analysis CSVs referenced in the manuscript.

Deviations and scope: the preregistration included multiple partitions (synthetic/emulation, community, production-like) and a preregistered sim-to-real confirmatory contrast. Deviation disclosure (explicit): the preregistered sim-to-real/production-like confirmatory comparison was not executed in this run; the executed confirmatory estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline evaluated on the synthetic/emulation partition only under shared_initial_candidate semantics. No manual post-lock edits of the manuscript’s technical content were performed.
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed and remain exploratory.

Deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties (syntax and prescribed workflow sequences) but did not measure broader semantic or behavioral correctness (protocol dynamics, emergent cross-device interactions).
Single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation were used; results do not establish multi-model or alternate-validator generality.
Only one automated repair attempt was permitted by design; multi-iteration repairs or human-in-the-loop escalation were not evaluated.
Adversarial and retrieval-based attacks (adaptive prompt-injection, vendor-targeted exploit vectors) and large-scale production heterogeneity were not exercised and remain open threats.
